en: to be degraded; to be demoted

examples.ko: 일 년 만에 부장에서 과장으로 강등됐어요.
examples.en: In just one year he was demoted from department head to section chief.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 성적이 나빠서 2부 리그로 강등될 것 같아요.
examples.en: Our team seems likely to be relegated to the second division because of poor results.
Nobody knows why he was demoted.
If your rank is lowered, your pay goes down too.

examples.ko: 그가 큰 실수를 해서 강등됐다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor that he made a big mistake and was demoted.
Even after being demoted, he worked hard.

explain: 사람의 직급이나 팀의 리그 등급이 내려갈 때 써요. 반대말은 '승진하다'(직급)나 '승격되다'(리그)예요. 억울한 느낌을 더하고 싶으면 '강등당하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: He was demoted because of a big mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 억울하거나 힘든 느낌을 더할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a feeling of unfairness or hardship.

phrases.example: 이번 시즌에는 우리 팀이 강등되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Our team wasn't relegated this season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내려가지 않고 자리를 지켰다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form meaning it kept its place.

phrases.en: The results are bad, so we're at risk of being demoted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 내려갈 수도 있는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a situation where a drop might happen.

explain_en: It is used when a person's rank or a team's league level goes down. The opposites are '승진하다' (rank) and '승격되다' (league). To add a sense of unfairness you can also say '강등당하다'.

en: to be performed; to be conducted

examples.en: The graduation ceremony is held in the auditorium.
The opening ceremony was held yesterday morning.

examples.ko: 내일 새 건물의 준공식이 거행될 거예요.
examples.en: The completion ceremony for the new building will be held tomorrow.
Because it rained, the event was held indoors.
I watched the awards ceremony being held in Seoul on TV.
The funeral is being held quietly.

explain: '거행되다'는 '열리다'보다 딱딱해요. 사람이 아니라 '식', '행사'가 주어일 때 써요. 사람이나 단체가 직접 치를 때는 '거행하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The graduation ceremony is held in the auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거행되다'보다 덜 딱딱한 말로, 일상에서 행사나 모임에 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A less formal word than 거행되다, used for events and gatherings in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The anniversary ceremony was held on a grand scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 화려한 식을 말할 때 '성대하게'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with '성대하게' (grandly) for large, splendid ceremonies.

phrases.example: 결혼식은 다음 주 토요일에 거행될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The wedding is scheduled to take place next Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 열릴 식이나 행사를 알릴 때 쓰는 미래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A future form used to announce an upcoming ceremony or event.

explain_en: 거행되다 is stiffer than 열리다 for an event being held. The subject is the ceremony itself, such as 식 or 행사. When a person or group does the holding, 거행하다 is used instead.

p.n: 공연되다 is for shows, not ceremonies.

en: to be designed; to be invented; to be created

examples.ko: 이 의자는 허리가 아픈 사람을 위해 고안됐어요.
examples.en: This chair was designed for people with back pain.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 백 년 전에 고안되었어요.
examples.en: This method was devised a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 쉽게 쓸 수 있도록 고안된 앱이에요.
examples.en: It's an app designed to be easy to use.
I'm curious how this kind of tool was invented.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 고안되면 많은 사람이 도움을 받을 거예요.
examples.en: If a new system is devised, many people will be helped.

examples.ko: 처음에는 놀이로 고안돼서 지금까지 전해 와요.
examples.en: It was first devised as a game and has been passed down until now.

explain: '고안하다'의 받는 쪽 말로, 만든 사람이 아니라 만들어진 물건이나 방법에 초점을 맞춰요. '~을/를 위해 고안되다'는 제품 소개나 설명서에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This tool was made for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고안되다'보다 쉽고 일상적이에요. 새로 궁리했다는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than 고안되다, but with less of a feeling of newly thought-out design.

phrases.example: 이 방법은 어린이를 위해 고안된 방법이에요.
phrases.en: This is a method designed for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 말로, 방법이나 제품을 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies the following noun; often used when introducing a method or product.

phrases.example: 이 의자는 오래 앉아도 편하도록 새롭게 고안됐어요.
phrases.en: This chair was newly designed to be comfortable even when sitting for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이전에 없던 것이 처음 만들어졌다는 점을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes that something that didn't exist before was newly created.

explain_en: This is the receiving side of 고안하다: the focus is on the thing that was made, not the person who made it. '~을/를 위해 고안되다' (designed for ~) appears often in product descriptions and manuals.

examples.en: Try changing this sentence into the active voice.

examples.ko: 시험에 능동태와 피동태를 구별하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The exam had a question about telling active and passive voice apart.
In an active-voice sentence, the subject performs the action.
The teacher wrote active-voice example sentences on the board.

examples.ko: 이 책은 능동태와 피동태를 쉽게 설명해 줘요.
examples.en: This book explains active and passive voice in an easy way.

examples.ko: 능동태로 쓰면 글이 더 힘 있게 읽혀요.
examples.en: Writing in the active voice makes the text read more forcefully.

explain: 문법 수업이나 시험에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 나오지 않아요. 짝이 되는 말은 '피동태'(피동문)이에요.

phrases.en: In an active voice sentence, the subject acts directly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문법 설명에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in grammar explanations.

phrases.en: Try to tell active and passive voice apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대되는 짝 '피동태'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with its opposite, 피동태 (passive).

phrases.en: This text is mostly written in the active voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장을 어떤 형태로 썼는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what form a sentence is written in.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in the active voice

explain_en: This is a grammar-class and exam term that rarely comes up in everyday conversation. Its counterpart is '피동태' (passive voice).

en: to be closed (when a deadline passes or spots fill up)

examples.en: Applications closed yesterday.
Registration closes this evening.
Hand in the documents before it closes.
Recruitment had closed, so I couldn't apply.
I didn't know the event had closed.
Once registration closes, they don't accept anyone more.

explain: 마감하다는 사람이 끝내는 것이고, 마감되다는 시간이나 인원이 다 차서 저절로 끝나는 거예요. 명사 '마감'으로 '마감일', '마감 시간'처럼 더 많이 써요. 자리가 다 찼을 때도 '선착순 마감'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Apply before the spots are closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나기 전에 서두르라고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to urge someone to hurry before the cutoff.

phrases.en: You cannot sign up for a class that is already full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 신청이 끝난 것을 꾸며서 말하는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This modifier form describes something whose sign-up has already ended.

phrases.en: This class closes on a first-come, first-served basis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 온 사람부터 받다가 자리가 차면 끝난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means spots go to early arrivals and it closes once they are full.

explain_en: '마감하다' is something a person does to wrap things up, while '마감되다' happens by itself when time runs out or spots fill up. The noun '마감' is more common, as in '마감일' or '마감 시간'. Full spots are also called '선착순 마감'.

dis.h: reaches its deadline; no longer accepting

p.n: 마무리되다 says the process is wrapped up, not that a deadline cut it off.

en: to be quoted; to be cited

examples.en: That line is often quoted in books.
This paper has been cited in many studies.
We put quotation marks on the quoted parts.
I was surprised that my post was quoted in the news.
It's a problem if something is quoted without a source.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에 인용될 문장을 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Pick sentences to be quoted in the presentation.

explain: 다른 사람의 말이나 글, 자료가 내 글이나 발표 안에 가져와 쓰일 때 써요. 내가 가져다 쓰는 쪽은 '인용하다'예요. 보고서에서는 출처를 꼭 밝혀야 하고, 말로 옮길 때는 '그 사람이 이렇게 말했어요'처럼 쉽게 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 시는 노래 가사에 자주 인용돼요.
phrases.en: This poem is often quoted in song lyrics.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곳에서 반복해서 가져다 쓸 때 '자주'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '자주' is added when something is quoted repeatedly in many places.

phrases.en: Look up the source of the quoted words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인용된'으로 바꿔 가져다 쓴 말이나 글을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier '인용된' describes words or text that were quoted.

phrases.en: I quoted a sentence from a book in my report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가져다 쓰는 사람이 주어일 때는 '인용하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '인용하다' when the person doing the quoting is the subject.

explain_en: When someone else's words, writing or data are brought into another text or talk. The person who borrows it uses '인용하다'. Reports must name the source; in speech people simply say 'he said this'.

examples.en: The bank's computer network stopped, and work was paralyzed.
You need a password to log in to the school network.

examples.ko: 전산망 오류 때문에 표를 살 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't buy a ticket because of a network error.
They are replacing the government offices' computer network.

examples.ko: 전국 병원이 하나의 전산망으로 연결돼 있어요.
examples.en: Hospitals across the country are connected through a single computer network.

examples.ko: 전산망은 점검 시간에는 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: The network can't be used during maintenance hours.

explain: 은행, 학교, 관공서처럼 기관이 컴퓨터를 서로 이어 정보를 주고받는 시스템을 말해요. 누구나 쓰는 인터넷과 달리 기관 내부의 업무용 망이라는 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서 '전산'이라고만 해도 같은 뜻으로 써서, '전산 오류'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Registration is delayed because of a computer network error.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시스템에 문제가 생겼을 때 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in notices and news when a system has a problem.

phrases.en: The school built a new computer network.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 시스템을 새로 만든다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for an institution newly setting up a system.

phrases.example: 전산 문제 때문에 서류를 못 뗐어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't get the documents because of a computer system problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전산망 대신 짧게 말하는 일상적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short everyday way to say the same thing as 전산망.

explain_en: It refers to the system through which organizations such as banks, schools and government offices connect computers to exchange information. Unlike the public internet, it feels like an internal work network. In daily talk people also say just '전산' in the same sense, as in '전산 오류' (system error).

examples.en: I learned Darwin's theory of evolution at school.
I'm reading a book about the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 진화론은 생물이 환경에 맞게 변해 왔다고 설명해요.
examples.en: The theory of evolution explains that living things have changed to fit their environment.
There was a long debate over the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에서는 진화론을 쉽게 소개해 줘요.
examples.en: This museum introduces the theory of evolution in an easy way.

examples.ko: 진화론이 나오기 전에는 사람들이 다르게 생각했어요.
examples.en: Before the theory of evolution appeared, people thought differently.

explain: '진화'는 실제로 일어나는 변화를 말하고, '진화론'은 그 변화를 다룬 이론을 말해요. 그래서 '진화가 일어나다'처럼 쓰지만, 이론은 '진화론이 나오다', '진화론을 배우다'처럼 써요. 보통 '창조론'과 짝으로 나오고, '다윈의 진화론'처럼 사람 이름과 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: We learned about the theory of evolution in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업에서 이론을 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying the theory in class.
phrases.en_equiv: to learn the theory of evolution

phrases.en: Darwin put forward the theory of evolution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이론을 내세우는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person advancing the theory.
phrases.en_equiv: to advocate the theory of evolution

phrases.en: We debated the theory of evolution and creationism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말과 함께 두 생각을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired to compare the two views.

explain_en: '진화' is the change that actually happens, while '진화론' is the theory about that change. So you say '진화가 일어나다' for the change itself, but '진화론이 나오다' or '진화론을 배우다' for the theory. It often appears paired with '창조론' (creationism), and commonly with a person's name, as in '다윈의 진화론'.

en: to be started; to be commenced

examples.en: The new construction gets under way next week.
A week has passed since the investigation began.
Once the project starts, the team will get busy.
The recovery work began right away yesterday.
When the investigation began, people took notice.
There is only a plan; work hasn't begun yet.

explain: 착수되다는 공사, 조사, 수사, 연구처럼 큰일이 실제로 시작될 때 써요. '시작되다'보다 격식이 있고 공식적인 일에 어울려요. 파티나 수업이 시작될 때는 '시작되다'를 써요. 시작하는 쪽은 '착수하다'예요.

phrases.en: The new construction starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '착수되다'보다 덜 격식적이고 어떤 일에든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than 착수되다 and usable for any kind of event.

phrases.en: An investigation into the cause of the accident was launched right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사, 수사, 공사처럼 공식적인 일과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with official matters like investigations and construction.

phrases.example: 공사가 착수되기 전에 주민들에게 알려야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to notify residents before the construction begins.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 전에'와 연결해서 일이 시작되기 앞선 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connected with -기 전에 to talk about the time before the work begins.

explain_en: 착수되다 is used when a sizable job such as construction, an investigation or research actually begins. It is more formal than 시작되다 and suits official matters. For a party or a class starting, use 시작되다. The active form is 착수하다.

en: to be interpreted; to be comprehended; to be explained

examples.en: This sentence can be interpreted in two ways.
His words were interpreted as a refusal.
I wonder how dreams are interpreted.
The results may be interpreted differently.
It's an expression that doesn't read naturally when translated.
I corrected the content that had been misinterpreted.

explain: 말이나 글이 어떤 뜻으로 이해될 때 써요. '~로 해석되다'가 기본 틀이고, 같은 말을 사람마다 다르게 받아들일 때 자주 나와요. 다른 언어로 옮기는 것은 '번역되다'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: This poem is interpreted differently by each person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들이는 방식이 사람마다 다를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people understand something in different ways.

phrases.example: 그 말은 긍정적으로 해석될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: That remark can be interpreted positively.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~로 해석되다' 틀에 '긍정적으로'를 넣은 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ~로 해석되다 pattern with 긍정적으로 filled in.

phrases.en: This sentence is not easy to interpret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻을 이해하기 어려울 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when the meaning is hard to understand.

explain_en: Use it when words or writing get understood in a certain way. The basic frame is ~로 해석되다, and it often appears when people read the same thing differently. Moving it into another language is 번역되다, which is a separate word.
